title: Reliability collaboration 90-day operational charter
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working 90-day operational charter to align SRE, platform, serving-runtime, product, and solutions teams on a coordinated reliability program for model-serving surfaces (hosted API + dedicated).

Goals (90 days):
- Establish and publish SLOs for three priority APIs: generate (text), chat, and embeddings.
- Implement automated SLI collection and a test harness for SLO regression checks in CI.
- Define and validate an error-budget based rollback/traffic-shift runbook for canary/rollouts.
- Run two practical experiments to reduce tail latency: small-scale continuous-batching tuning and KV cache warmup strategy.

Context and why now:
Recent incidents showed correlated latency spikes during bursty traffic and model fallback periods. Product wants a predictable latency SLA for key customers; sales has asked for clear guardrails and an operational contract. This charter focuses on pragmatic, cross-team deliverables to move from ad-hoc monitoring to governed SLOs and operationalized error budgets.

Primary stakeholders and roles:
- SRE lead (owner): Maya Chen — program coordinator, SLO definitions, experiments oversight.
- Platform engineer: Liam Ortiz — metrics ingestion, long-term storage config, SLI alerts.
- Serving runtime lead: Sofia Patel — runtime telemetry hooks, KV cache changes, batching knobs.
- Observability/Telemetry: Diego Morales — dashboards, latency tail breakdowns, synthetic checks.
- Product PM: Evelyn Park — customer-facing SLO commitments, priority routing policy.
- Solutions Eng: Priya Nair (advisor) — early adopter feedback, customer playbooks.

High-level milestones and timelines:
- Week 0–2: Discovery sprint — map current signals, basic SLI inventory, choose measurement windows (rolling 5m for latency SLOs, 30d window for availability), and finalize SLO language.
- Week 3–4: Implement SLI collection plumbing for priority APIs (metrics, traces, synthetic probes). Create initial dashboards.
- Week 5–7: CI SLO regression harness — integrate three synthetic prompt sets, fail builds on large SLO regressions (alert-only initially).
- Week 8–9: Run two experiments (batching config + KV warmup) on staging and a small subset of traffic in canary. Collect data.
- Week 10–12: Define error-budget policy, runbook for rollback/fallback, and publish a cross-team on-call playbook. Prepare customer-facing SLO page draft.

Concrete SLO proposals (draft — to be finalized in Week 1):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% successful request rate (status code + inference-complete) measured over 30d rolling window for hosted generate endpoints.
- Latency SLOs: P95 < 200ms, P99 < 700ms for short-sequence (<=128 tokens) paths; P95 < 600ms for long-sequence (>=512 tokens) paths. Use 5m rolling windows aggregated into 30d for breach calculations.
- Embeddings SLO: P95 < 120ms for typical vector size 1536.
Notes: these targets are intentionally conservative — we want realistic, achievable baselines for the error budget experiments.

Measurement definitions (SLI specifics):
- Success definition: request completes with final token(s) returned OR embedding vector returned within measurement boundary (we will instrument per-request finalizer).
- Latency: time from API gateway accept to first-byte and to final-byte. SLO will use final-byte for generation and embedding completion.
- Exclusions: planned maintenance windows, deploys where canary intentionally forces degraded mode; customer-requested rate limits.

Error budget and rollout policy (draft):
- Each service gets a monthly error budget (1 - SLO). When cumulative exceedance > 50% of monthly error budget, we trigger an operations review and freeze on risky rollouts for 72 hours.
- Canary rule: reduce canary traffic to 5% if P99 breaches by >2x baseline for 10 minutes; auto-rollback to previous model variant if sustained >30 minutes.

Experiments — brief plans and success criteria:
1) Continuous batching knob sweep (serving-runtime):
   - What: tune max batch size, flush latency thresholds, and per-model batching windows; measure effect on P95 and token cost.
   - Success: reduce P95 by >=15% on tail-heavy workload without >10% increase in cost per token.
   - Owner: Sofia + platform infra (Liam).

2) KV cache warmup strategy (prefix caching):
   - What: pre-warm KV cache for high-traffic prompt prefixes and implement cache-priming during model warmup.
   - Success: reduce P99 access latency by >=20% during burst start-up windows.
   - Owner: Serving runtime + Observability (Sofia, Diego).

Runbooks and playbooks to create:
- Canary degradation playbook (traffic reduction, model fallback, alerts to execute).
- Incident triage runbook specific to model-serving latency anomalies (checklist, tracing queries, common root causes).
- Error budget review agenda and postmortem template (short-format for ops cadence).

Observability and tooling needs:
- New metrics: request_finalized boolean, end_to_end_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate_by_prefix, batch_size_distribution.
- Traces: include model-variant, GPU-queue-time, kernel-selection-tag in spans.
- Dashboards: per-model and per-route SLO burn rate, week-to-week regression diff, canary vs. baseline comparison panel.
- CI harness: synthetic prompt sets (short-gen, chat-multi-turn, large-embedding) stored as fixtures.

Dependencies and risks:
- Platform metrics ingestion latency — currently some metrics arrive with seconds-level jitter; may affect short-window SLOs. Mitigation: use longer aggregation windows for early release and track ingestion lag as a metric.
- Model variability: upstream model changes can shift token-level compute; require gating on model-variant schema and add model-variance flag in CI.
- Capacity constraints: experiments may require reserved dedicated GPU capacity; coordinate with Dedicated team for burst tickets.

Communication plan and cadence:
- Weekly reliability sync (30m) — owners only; Monday standup to report experimental progress and SLO deltas.
- Biweekly stakeholder review (1h) — product, SRE, platform, sales (brief customer impact summary).
- Public draft SLO page (internal): end of Week 12 for internal review; external-facing SLOs only after legal and product sign-off.

Unresolved questions / notes to self:
- Need decision on exact measurement window for P99 (5m vs 15m) — tradeoff: sensitivity vs noise. Propose 5m for alerts, 15m for enforcement.
- Confirm which deploy events are auto-excluded from SLOs (hotfix vs scheduled).
- Do we want to include function/tool-calls as part of same surface or leave for phase 2?

Immediate actions (next 7 days):
- Week 0 action list:
  [ ] Finalize SLO wording in this doc and send to stakeholders for comment (Maya).
  [ ] Create JIRA epic and sub-tasks for SLI plumbing and CI harness (Liam).
  [ ] Add synthetic prompt fixtures to repo and stub CI job (Diego).
  [ ] Schedule 1:1 with Serving Runtime to scope batching experiment (Sofia).

Appendix: quick checklist for SLO review meeting:
- Confirm SLI definitions and exclusion list
- Review initial dashboards and ingestion lag metric
- Agree on error-budget thresholds and handoff triggers
- Validate canary rollback policy and responsible oncall

This doc is intentionally a working draft — add comments inline, drop unresolved questions, and update owners where needed.

Last editors: Maya Chen, Liam Ortiz, Sofia Patel.
